result:
The task is complete. I implemented the three missing operations in `WindowStats.calr`, following the existing `WindowSum` conventions (mutable bindings, `§WH` loops, `§Q` preconditions, `§IDX`/`§LEN` idioms):

1. **`WindowMin`** — seeds the minimum from the first window element, then scans the rest, keeping the smallest. Carries the same `start >= 0`, `count > 0`, `start + count <= §LEN values` preconditions. Works with negative elements.

2. **`MaxWindowSum`** — computes `WindowSum` for every valid start index (`0` through `len - count`) and keeps the largest. Preconditions `count > 0` and `count <= §LEN values`. Seeds `best` from the first window so an all-negative array correctly yields a negative result rather than 0.

3. **`CountAbove`** — counts windows whose sum is strictly greater than `threshold`. The loop guard `(<= (+ start count) §LEN values)` naturally produces 0 windows when `count` exceeds the array length. Precondition `count > 0`, and postcondition `§S (>= result 0)` pins the never-negative guarantee.

`WindowSum` was left unchanged. All Calor checks (compile, contracts, effects, references) passed, and `dotnet build` succeeds with 0 warnings / 0 errors.
